title: Mohamud, Guterres Discuss AUSSOM Support at UN General Assembly
detail: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud met UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres in New York on September 24, 2026 during the high-level week of the 81st UN General Assembly session to discuss security developments in Somalia and continued international backing for AUSSOM. Guterres 'reaffirmed the United Nations' commitment to Somalia's key national priorities,' according to a readout of the meeting, though no new funding commitments or agreements were announced. Current AUSSOM and UNSOS mandates expire December 31, 2026; the US has separately proposed a 12-month drawdown of UNSOS beginning January 2027 rather than an immediate cutoff, with final timelines to be set during UN Security Council deliberations in December.

media.caption: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud meets UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to discuss AUSSOM support, New York, Sep 24, 2026

title: Mohamud Tells UN General Assembly Somalia Needs 'Predictable, Sustainable' Support for AU Mission
detail: Addressing the UN General Assembly's general debate on September 24, 2026, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud called for 'predictable, sustainable support for Somalia's security transition, including adequate financing for an African Union mission in Somalia,' amid the funding crisis facing AUSSOM and UNSOS. He warned that disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz had caused 'serious economic and humanitarian consequences' for import-dependent Somalia, and called for UN Security Council reform, saying 'Africa remains unrepresented in the permanent category' and urging 'meaningful representation in both categories of the council.' On climate change, he said more than 40% of the global population is vulnerable to its destructive effects, with developing nations spending disproportionate shares of GDP responding to climate impacts. Mohamud also reaffirmed Somalia's support for Palestinian statehood along 1967 borders.

media.caption: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud addresses the UN General Assembly's 81st session general debate, Sep 24, 2026

title: Unverified Reports of Macawisley Mobilization in Hiiraan Amid Hirshabelle Election Dispute
detail: A political dispute over Hirshabelle State's local council and parliamentary elections, scheduled for September 30, 2026 by the National Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission, intensified in Hiiraan region on September 24, 2026, with unverified reports of a possible mobilization of Macawisley clan militia fighters in the Afcad area opposing the vote. The reports did not include verified details on fighter numbers, weapons, or command. Hirshabelle Vice President Yusuf Hagar Dabageed said elections should not proceed without a political agreement addressing the Hawadle community's expectations for the next state presidency, and accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of abandoning prior understandings; the Hawadle community itself is divided, with the Hawadle Political Council backing incumbent Hirshabelle President Ali Abdullahi Hussein 'Guudlaawe' for re-election. The dispute follows a September 7, 2026 attack on a Beledweyne voter-registration center by suspected Macawisley gunmen that killed one person, and a large protest in Beledweyne opposing the vote without a prior political deal.
